transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-19
Start: 10:00 AM PST
End: 11:02 AM PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Tina Morales, Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Jamal Ortiz, Lina Park, Omar Vasquez
Agenda: 1) Surface knife-edge risks for the 2.0.4 release; 2) Decide canary gating thresholds; 3) Close outstanding incident retro items related to memory regressions

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Team validated deploy window and most gating metrics; remaining unknown is KV-cache thrash under long-seq traffic and an intermittent OOM seen on 16GB nodes.
- Agreement: start canary at 1% for 30m, then 5% for 60m with strict p95/p99 thresholds; rollback triggers defined.
- Action owners assigned for smoke tests, alerting, and rollback docs.

--- Transcript (timestamps approx every 30-90s; transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Tina: alright, thanks folks for being on time, let's kick off. we have a fairly tight window today, uh - main goal is to call out any knife-edge risks before we greenlight the canary tomorrow.
[00:22] Alex: quick run through of the release content - 2.0.4 includes kernel selection change, improved batching heuristics, and a small change to cache eviction behavior for prefix caching. nothing user-visible except lower cost in most workloads.
[00:35] Priya: mhm, and the kernel change is that we prefer the fused attention path on Ampere variants, but with longer sequence lengths we sometimes fall back to a generic kernel which can raise memory by about 10-15%. we've seen that on a couple of internal traces.
[00:58] Jamal: to be clear, the OOMs we tracked in staging were on 16G instances with long chat history, right? there's a pattern around kv cache growth + blob growth.
[01:15] Priya: yeah, it's the KV cache across multiple segments + our new slice compaction had a bug where it didn't free a slot under certain edge cases. we fixed it in the branch but still want to smoke test. sorry, i said 'kv cash' in a ticket earlier, that was me.
[01:34] Lina: haha noted. ok so risk list so far: memory regression (intermittent), p99 latency spikes with the kernel fallback, and slight cost delta if batching heuristics misfire under small request sizes.
[01:50] Omar: timeline reminder - deploy window 02/20 02:00 UTC, we have a 3-hour rollover. canary first, then ramp. need sign-off by EOW.
[02:05] Alex: i'd propose canary 1% for 30m, then 5% for 60m, then 25% for 30m if healthy. thresholds: p95 increase <= 15% from baseline, p99 increase <= 25%, and no new OOMs. if any critical alert fires, immediate rollback.
[02:30] Priya: are we comfortable with the p99 threshold? that feels permissive if fallback happens. perhaps set p99 delta <= 20% and add an absolute floor: p99 must be < 1.2s for seq <512.
[02:49] Jamal: we should also watch memory headroom per GPU across the canary set; add a custom alert: mem_util% > 88% sustained for 2m triggers paging.
[03:05] Tina: good, add that. also ensure that the dashboard surfaces kernel-fallback counts and last-fallback-timestamp. that was useful during the last kernel incident.
[03:22] Priya: quick note, fallback counts are slightly noisy because some models intentionally fall back for fp16 quantized layers; we'll tag the counts with model-variant to make them actionable.
[03:40] Alex: what's our rollback plan? immediate traffic cut to previous model variant in the same pool or route to smaller model?
[03:52] Omar: primary rollback is traffic cut to previous model variant via routing rule (fast). secondary is scale-up of Dedicated pool if we see transient errors, but that takes time. tertiary is model swap to a 7B variant to preserve availability.
[04:12] Jamal: make sure runbook has contact list and the exact kubernetes patch to revert the config. last time someone had to remember flags, and that slowed us.
[04:26] Tina: agreed. action: Omar publish runbook with the exact kubectl apply -f snippet.
[04:34] Priya: on the KV cache thrash — i ran a synthetic where multiple sessions with 2-3k prefix tokens thrash the cache and we saw memory climb before GC could reclaim. mitigation options: faster compaction, set per-session prefix caps, or aggressive eviction for canary traffic.
[04:58] Jamal: could we also enable a temporary config to pin max sequence len at 1024 for canary? seems heavy-handed but reduces risk.
[05:12] Priya: yes we can, but that reduces quality for long chats. maybe we add a canary flag: prefix_cap=800 and compaction aggressive=true.
[05:26] Alex: let's list trade-offs in the release notes. we need to flag that canary may degrade responses >800 tokens slightly. customers with long-history will see truncated contexts.
[05:43] Lina: we need comms to SRE and to customers in the internal beta - that goes to the partners slack and the stakeholder email. Alex you'll own comms?
[05:55] Alex: yes, i'll draft.
[06:02] [cross-talk] Tina: mm-hmm.
[06:10] Priya: one more technical unknown: the new batching heuristics have a fallback path when token arrival rate is bursty; that code path isn't exercised in our standard unit tests. we should run bursty traffic replay.
[06:28] Jamal: i'll set up a replay job from the replay-runner cluster, 5-min bursts at 80% of prod qps to exercise it. schedule tonight?
[06:39] Priya: yea, and include long-seq traces.
[06:44] Omar: action: Jamal run replay + post results link.
[06:49] Alex: regarding metrics, what dashboards do we monitor? p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, model mem usage, kernel-fallback rate, error rate (5xx), cost-per-token delta. is anything missing?
[07:05] Priya: add kv-cache size and compaction rate. and also a count of 'prefix-truncate' events.
[07:15] Jamal: we should have an SLO-based alert: if error budget burn rate > 200% over a 1h window, pause rollout.
[07:27] Tina: yes, amending: error budget burn > 150% triggers a manual pause and exec.
[07:35] [00:08 in meeting? transcription timestamps drift but continue] Alex: small shout — we also need to validate the third party library bump (tensor-kernel 4.12) doesn't regress perf on older cards. regression matrix is in the spreadsheet: link: https://redwood.app/rl/release-matrix-2-0-4 (note: link auto-summarized)
[07:58] Priya: i've run the matrix on A100 and T4, but not on older V100 setups in the lab. there's a small perf delta on V100 that we should measure; it's likely due to a different cuBLAS kernel selection.
[08:18] Jamal: let's not block release for V100 unless it affects customers in prod region; check deployment regions and customer usage.
[08:30] Lina: i can pull region usage quickly.
[08:34] Alex: on incident retro items — last memory regression had three open follow-ups: 1) better regression test for long-seq, 2) automated alert on memory spike, 3) postmortem doc completion. which are still open?
[08:48] Priya: 1) partial, test exists but not integrated; 2) in progress (Jamal), 3) doc is a draft.
[08:55] Jamal: i updated alerting rules but need to tune thresholds (open item).
[09:02] Tina: okay, closure expectation: get those done pre-canary or have mitigation in place. Priya, can you land the compaction fix in the hotfix branch and tag for canary?
[09:14] Priya: yes, i'll push a patch today. it's low-risk.
[09:18] Omar: can we add a canary-specific feature flag to turn off the new slice compaction? fallback option.
[09:26] Priya: yep, we have feature-flag support. can make it on by default for canary and keep off for a short test.
[09:34] Alex: we keep the flag but default to ON? i'm worried about not testing the new code in canary. maybe default ON and have a fast revert flag.
[09:45] Priya: makes sense.
[09:48] [10:00 mark] Tina: okay summary checkpoint — agreed items: run extended canary smoke with long-seq; add memory and fallback alerts; publish rollback runbook; set canary ramp 1% -> 5% -> 25% with thresholds discussed.
[10:05] Lina: comms: draft to eng-announce and partners slack; include the caveats about prefix-cap=800.
[10:12] Omar: timeline check again: publish runbook 02/20 00:00 UTC? earlier you said 02/20 02:00 UTC deploy window; docs ideally by 02/20 00:00 UTC.
[10:24] Alex: i'll send the stakeholder mail by 02/19 6pm PST.
[10:29] Jamal: for alerts, add a synthetic test to alert if kernel-fallback rate increases 3x in 5m. that's better than absolute counts.
[10:40] Priya: agreed. and let's tag the spiking traces for faster triage.
[10:46] [cross-talk / agreement] Tina: wrap up — any other risks?
[10:50] Priya: one small one: quant ops in the 4.12 bump could change inference determinism, might affect eval suites.
[10:58] Alex: note to run eval harness across nightly before canary.
[11:02] Tina: cool. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene in the morning if anything pops.

- Owners and action items assigned (see action_items).
